decisions.thought: Team preview: mirror match. Bringing Incineroar (lead, Intimidate and Fake Out), Garchomp (Mega threat, fastest attacker), and Gholdengo (Life Orb special sweeper). Opponent is a scripted bot with my team's exact sets. Watch for Mega Garchomp and Gholdengo threats. Keep Kingambit and the others in back.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick a team against a mirror matchup. Garchomp, Incineroar, and Gholdengo stand out as strong picks, with mega Garchomp especially solid against the opponent's own Garchomp. I'm weighing whether Kingambit might fit better than one of these depending on their likely composition.

So I'll go with Incineroar as the lead, backed by Garchomp and Gholdengo.

decisions.thought: Mirror match vs a bot copying my team. Opposing Corviknight has Mirror Armor, so my Intimidate and any stat drops bounce back to me. Incineroar's Flare Blitz is super effective on Corviknight (Steel weakness). Fake Out does little here, so I'm using Flare Blitz for damage. Watch for Kingambit (Defiant/Supreme Overlord), Gholdengo (Life Orb-style threat) and Garchomp (Mega or Sand Veil). Garchomp is my fastest attacker. Keep Gholdengo for special damage.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: On turn one, Incineroar faces Corviknight: Fake Out is only weakly effective since Steel resists Normal, but Flare Blitz hits hard as a Fire move against the Flying/Steel type, though I need to check how Mirror Armor interacts with any stat drops involved.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is at 112/202 with lowered attack from the intimidate swap, while the opposing Incineroar just came in at full health and their Corviknight is sitting at 46% in reserve. I'm weighing whether to switch into Garchomp, full health with Mega available, since its ground-type moves would hit the opposing Incineroar hard.

Flare Blitz feels weak here since Fire resists Fire, but Parting Shot could let me drop their stats while safely bringing in Garchomp or Gholdengo, even though another intimidate hit would drop Garchomp's attack again.

So Gholdengo isn't great against Incineroar, and Garchomp's Earthquake is just neutral. Maybe Parting Shot is the better play, lowering Incineroar's offenses to switch Garchomp in more safely, even though Garchomp still eats the intimidate drop.

decisions.thought: Garchomp is out at full HP against Corviknight (46%, Mirror Armor, Roost). Earthquake does nothing to Flying types, so I'm using Mega Stone Edge, which is super effective on Flying and has high crit chance, to try to finish it. Mega Garchomp also sets up a stronger attacker for later. Gholdengo is down and Incineroar (healthy-ish, Intimidate) is the threat. Mirror Armor reflects my stat drops back, so avoid relying on Intimidate or Parting Shot against Corviknight. Kingambit and Sinistcha are still unseen.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking Garchomp's matchup against Corviknight: Earthquake is useless since Flying types are immune to Ground, Dragon Claw isn't very effective against Steel, and Stone Edge ends up neutral since the 2x against Flying is canceled by the 0.5x against Steel.

Running the damage math, Stone Edge lands around 59 and Dragon Claw around 34 against Corviknight's ~88 HP, so neither move threatens a one-shot even with a Mega Garchomp boost. I'm also noting that Mirror Armor doesn't interfere with Swords Dance since that's a self-buff, not a stat drop inflicted on the opponent.

Checking Corviknight's retaliation options, Brave Bird and its Steel-type moves don't hit Garchomp especially hard given the Dragon/Ground typing. With a possible Incineroar switch-in where Garchomp has the advantage, Mega Evolving now and firing off Stone Edge seems like the strongest play, netting roughly 67 damage with the boosted Attack stat.

decisions.thought: Garchomp Mega (158 Spe) outspeeds everything they showed except possibly fast Corviknight. Corviknight (69%, Mirror Armor, Roost) is hard to dent: Earthquake does nothing to Flying, and Dragon Claw is resisted. Swords Dance now sets up for later; Mirror Armor only reflects drops, not boosts. If Incineroar comes in, Earthquake hits it for super effective damage and the Attack boost offsets Intimidate. Watch for Kingambit and Sinistcha.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Corviknight sits at 69% of roughly 189 max HP, around 130 HP remaining, while Mega Garchomp's Speed of 158 outpaces it. With 222 Attack and a STAB Stone Edge at 100 base power despite its 80% accuracy and solid crit chance, I'm estimating it could deal somewhere around 60-70% of Corviknight's health, super effective against its Flying typing.

Actually, reconsidering the typing: Corviknight is Flying/Steel, so Rock's 2x against Flying gets cut in half by Steel's resistance to Rock, making Stone Edge just neutral damage overall. Dragon Claw would be resisted by Steel, and Earthquake is useless since Flying types are immune to Ground — so none of Garchomp's moves actually land super effectively here. Given that, Stone Edge remains the best damage option, though Corviknight will likely just Roost again to heal back up; Swords Dance followed by a stronger Stone Edge next turn could be the better play.

Swords Dance also sets up well against a possible Incineroar switch-in — its Intimidate would cut my boosted attack, but Garchomp still outspeeds and can hit it hard with Earthquake since Fire types take double Ground damage. So I'll go with Swords Dance now while Corviknight is the only real threat on the field.

decisions.thought: Garchomp Mega (+2 Atk) is the main attacker. Corviknight (72%, Mirror Armor, Roost, Shell Bell, Body Press) is the target. decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking Stone Edge's effectiveness against Corviknight's Flying/Steel typing—super effective against Flying but resisted by Steel, so they cancel out to neutral damage overall.

With Garchomp at +2 Attack, Stone Edge should still deal roughly 228+ damage with STAB, likely enough to knock out Corviknight at 72% HP, especially factoring in crit chance. Dragon Claw and Earthquake are both weak or useless here, so Stone Edge is the clear choice.
